questions.stem: A motor vehicle battery differs from a torch battery mainly because the vehicle battery
options: produces alternating current for the starter
is used only once and then thrown away
is rechargeable and can deliver a very large current
gives exactly 1.5 V in every model and size of vehicle
questions.explanation: A lead-acid vehicle battery is a secondary cell that is recharged by the alternator and can supply hundreds of amperes for cranking.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the battery in a motor vehicle?
options: Supplying current to the starter motor
Powering lights when the engine is stopped
Steadying the voltage of the electrical system
Supplying the ignition system during starting
Converting a.c. from the alternator into d.c.
questions.explanation: Rectification is done by the alternator's diode pack, not by the battery.

questions.topic: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
questions.stem: Each cell of a lead-acid battery has a nominal voltage of about 2 V. The number of cells in a 12 V battery is
questions.explanation: 12 V / 2 V per cell = 6 cells connected in series.

questions.topic: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
questions.stem: A technician cuts open a scrap but fully charged lead-acid battery and finds chocolate-brown plates. These plates are the
options: negative plates, made of spongy lead
positive plates, made of lead dioxide
negative plates, coated with lead sulphate
positive plates, made of pure antimony
questions.explanation: Charged positive plates are lead dioxide, PbO2, which is chocolate brown; negative plates are grey spongy lead.

questions.topic: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
questions.stem: A battery rated 60 Ah at the 20-hour rate should be able to deliver a steady current of
questions.explanation: Capacity / time = 60 Ah / 20 h = 3 A.

questions.stem: When preparing battery electrolyte, the correct practice is to
options: pour water quickly into the concentrated acid to save time
pour the acid slowly into the water while stirring
mix acid and water in a metal bucket
heat the water first to speed up mixing
add salt to the water before the acid
questions.explanation: Adding water to concentrated acid can boil and spit acid; acid is always added slowly to water in a glass or plastic vessel.

questions.stem: A discharged 45 Ah battery is put on a constant-current charge of 4.5 A. Allowing 25% extra for charging losses, the charging time needed is about
The instrument used to measure the specific gravity of battery electrolyte is the
questions.explanation: A hydrometer float shows the relative density of the electrolyte, which indicates state of charge.

questions.stem: A car that has stood for three weeks will not crank. Every cell of its battery gives a hydrometer reading of about 1.12 and the readings are within 0.01 of one another. The correct action is to
options: replace the battery at once because one cell is dead
add concentrated acid to every cell
pour away the electrolyte and refill with water
recharge the battery and retest it
questions.explanation: Uniform low readings near 1.12 mean the whole battery is discharged, not that a cell is faulty; it should be recharged and retested.

questions.stem: An idle battery that will be stored for some weeks should be
options: left discharged so that it will not overheat
drained of its electrolyte and stored upside down
kept on the bare floor in a damp corner of the store
charged, kept cool and dry, and recharged regularly
connected to a load to keep it working
questions.explanation: A battery left discharged sulphates; it should be stored charged and refreshed regularly.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of starting system
questions.stem: A driver turns the key and hears the engine being turned over but it does not fire. Which system has done its job correctly?
questions.explanation: The starter cranks the engine to the minimum speed at which it can fire and run on its own.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of starting system
questions.stem: The solenoid in a starting system
options: lets a small switch current control the heavy starter current
stores electrical energy for cranking until the key is turned again
controls the charging rate of the battery
questions.explanation: The solenoid is an electromagnetic switch (and often engages the pinion) so that the ignition switch carries only a small current.

questions.stem: On a starting circuit diagram, the thin wire marked "50" or "S" connects the ignition switch to the
questions.explanation: Terminal 50 (S) feeds the solenoid pull-in and hold-in windings when the key is turned to START; the heavy cable goes to the main terminal.

questions.stem: Which starter type has a pinion that is thrown out of mesh as soon as the engine fires and spins the ring gear faster than the armature?
options: Permanent-magnet pre-engaged type with reduction gears
questions.explanation: In the inertia drive the faster ring gear screws the pinion back along its helix and out of mesh.

questions.stem: Diesel engines are usually fitted with pre-engaged rather than inertia starters because the pre-engaged type
options: draws no current at all from the battery during cranking
meshes the pinion before full current flows
has no armature, brushes or commutator to wear out
disengages itself the moment the starter current begins to flow
turns the crankshaft directly without needing a ring gear
questions.explanation: In the pre-engaged type the solenoid pushes the pinion into mesh first, reducing gear wear and preventing premature ejection on high-compression engines.

questions.stem: After a starter commutator has been skimmed, the insulation between the segments is cut slightly below the copper. This operation is called
questions.explanation: Undercutting keeps the mica/insulation below the copper surface so it does not lift the brushes as the copper wears.

questions.stem: A growler is used when repairing starter motors to test the
options: battery for specific gravity of the electrolyte
pinion for worn or chipped teeth
questions.explanation: A shorted armature coil placed on a growler causes a hacksaw blade held over it to vibrate.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of ignition system
questions.stem: High-tension current in a contact-breaker system flows: coil tower, HT king lead, ______, plug lead, spark plug. The missing item is the
questions.explanation: The rotor arm turns inside the distributor cap and passes HT current to each plug lead in firing order.

questions.stem: In the ignition circuit, the primary winding of the coil is connected between the ignition switch and the
options: spark plugs through the HT lead
questions.explanation: The low-tension primary circuit runs battery – switch – coil primary – contact breaker – earth.

questions.topic: Construction and operation of ignition coil
questions.stem: An ignition coil steps 12 V up to high voltage mainly because its secondary winding has
options: fewer turns of thick wire than the primary winding
the same number of turns as the primary
far more turns than the primary
a permanent magnet instead of a core
questions.explanation: A high secondary-to-primary turns ratio, together with rapid collapse of the field, induces a very high voltage.

questions.topic: Construction and operation of ignition coil
questions.stem: A replacement coil must give 24 kV at the plug when a self-induced e.m.f. of 240 V appears across its 180-turn primary. Ignoring losses, the number of secondary turns needed is
questions.explanation: Ns = Np x Vs/Vp = 180 x 24 000/240 = 18 000 turns.

questions.stem: In a breakerless electronic ignition system, the job done by the contact breaker in older cars is performed by a
options: pulse generator (magnetic or Hall-effect sensor) and transistor module
questions.explanation: A pulse generator signals the electronic module, whose power transistor switches the coil primary current, so there are no points to wear.

questions.stem: If the spark occurs too late in the compression stroke, the engine is said to have
questions.explanation: A late spark is retarded timing, causing loss of power, overheating and high fuel use.

questions.stem: A taxi driver in Enugu complains of a metallic rattle from the engine whenever he climbs a steep hill at full throttle. The timing fault MOST likely responsible is
options: a weak battery that cannot hold voltage
a faulty fuel gauge sender unit
a blown headlamp fuse in the fuse box
questions.explanation: Too much advance makes peak pressure occur early, causing detonation heard as pinking.

questions.stem: Which instrument is most suitable for checking whether there is continuity in a high-tension lead?
questions.explanation: Continuity and resistance are measured with an ohmmeter.

questions.stem: A loud bang from the exhaust when the ignition is switched off at speed (backfiring) may be caused by
options: too much oil in the sump splashing onto the hot crankshaft
unburnt mixture igniting in a hot exhaust
questions.explanation: Unburnt fuel reaching the hot exhaust ignites there, causing backfire; timing and mixture faults are typical causes.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of charging system
questions.stem: If the voltage regulator of a car failed so that full field current flowed all the time, the MOST likely result would be
options: the starter motor refusing to turn the engine
the fuel gauge reading empty all the time
overcharging and boiling of the battery
the head lamps going out completely at once
questions.explanation: The regulator limits field current; without it the alternator voltage rises too high and overcharges the battery.

questions.stem: In an alternator, the brushes rub on the slip rings in order to feed current to the
questions.explanation: Brushes and slip rings carry the small field current into the rotating rotor winding; output comes from the stationary stator.

questions.stem: The alternator output is converted from a.c. to d.c. by
options: the slip rings and carbon brushes
questions.explanation: Silicon diodes in a bridge allow current to flow in one direction only.

questions.stem: A technician finds that one of the six main rectifier diodes in an alternator has gone open circuit. The MOST likely effect is
options: no effect at all on the output
the alternator producing pure a.c. at the terminal
the battery discharging through the stator when parked
questions.explanation: With one diode open, one half of one phase is lost: output falls and ripple increases. A shorted diode, not an open one, lets the battery discharge.

questions.stem: Diagrams are used to represent charging circuits mainly because they
options: make the circuit cheaper to produce
increase the output of the alternator
replace the need for test instruments
show the true size of each part
show how parts connect so faults are traced
questions.explanation: Circuit diagrams show how components are connected so that technicians can follow and test the circuit.

questions.stem: The ignition (charge) warning light stays on with the engine running fast. The MOST likely fault is
questions.explanation: If the alternator is not turning or not charging, the warning lamp stays lit.

questions.stem: When testing an alternator diode with a multimeter on the diode range, a good diode should show
questions.explanation: A healthy diode conducts in forward bias only; reading both ways means shorted, neither way means open.

questions.topic: Purpose and classification of lighting in a motor vehicle
questions.stem: A road safety officer stops a lorry at night. The lorry would be breaking the law if it were driving without its
questions.explanation: Lights required by law include head, side, tail, stop, number plate and indicator lights.

questions.stem: In a quartz-halogen head lamp bulb, the filament life is extended because
options: the bulb works at a low temperature
the halogen redeposits tungsten on the filament
the filament is made of copper
the glass is painted black inside
the lamp contains no gas at all
questions.explanation: The halogen cycle redeposits tungsten on the filament and keeps the glass clear.

questions.stem: Head lamp beam setting should be checked with the vehicle
options: loaded with heavy goods on the roof rack and boot
unladen, level and at correct tyre pressures
questions.explanation: Correct setting needs the vehicle level, at the right load and tyre pressure, so that beams are aimed accurately.

questions.stem: Two 55 W head lamp bulbs are supplied from a 12 V system. The current through the head lamp fuse is about

questions.topic: Maintenance and repairs of lighting system
questions.stem: Both head lamps fail together but the side lights work. The FIRST check should be the
questions.explanation: A common fault affecting both lamps is in the shared supply: fuse, relay or switch.

questions.topic: Constructional details and operation of auxiliary system components
questions.stem: In a windscreen wiper motor, the "park" switch ensures that the blades
options: stop at the bottom of the screen
sweep faster when it rains heavily
move only when the engine is running
stop in whatever position the switch is turned off
questions.explanation: The park (limit) switch keeps the motor running after switch-off until the blades reach the rest position.

questions.topic: Maintenance and repairs of auxiliary components
questions.stem: The fuel gauge needle stays at FULL even when the tank is nearly empty. The fault is MOST likely
options: an earthed sender lead or stuck float
questions.explanation: In many gauges a grounded sender wire or jammed float gives a permanently full reading.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe how a hydrometer is used to test a lead-acid battery. [5 marks]
(b) State three symptoms of over-charging a battery. [3 marks]
(c) A 12 V battery shows cell readings of 1.27, 1.27, 1.26, 1.10, 1.27 and 1.26. State, with reason, what this indicates and what should be done. [4 marks]
(d) State three safety precautions when charging batteries. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) remove vent plugs
1 mark: (a) squeeze bulb, insert nozzle into cell
1 mark: (a) release bulb to draw electrolyte so float rides freely
1 mark: (a) read at eye level the mark at liquid surface
1 mark: (a) return electrolyte to same cell; repeat for each cell
3 marks: (b) any three: excessive gassing/bubbling, overheating, loss of water, buckled plates, corrosion of terminals (1 each)
2 marks: (c) one cell (1.10) much lower than others: that cell is faulty/shorted (difference above about 0.05)
2 marks: (c) recharge and retest; if still low, replace battery
3 marks: (d) any three: ventilated area, no naked flame/sparks, switch off charger before connecting/disconnecting, wear goggles/gloves, correct polarity (1 each)
questions.explanation: The hydrometer draws electrolyte so the float reads specific gravity. Over-charging shows as gassing, heat and water loss. A single cell at 1.10 with others near 1.27 indicates a defective cell; recharge and retest, then replace if it stays low. Charge in ventilation, avoid sparks, switch off before connecting, wear PPE.

questions.stem:
(a) With the aid of a labelled description, explain the operation of a pre-engaged starter motor. [7 marks]
(b) Distinguish between the axial and inertia types of starter motor. [4 marks]
(c) State four faults that can prevent a starter motor from cranking the engine. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) ignition key energises solenoid pull-in and hold-in windings
2 marks: (a) plunger moves; engagement lever pushes pinion along shaft into mesh with ring gear
1 mark: (a) plunger closes main contacts at end of travel
1 mark: (a) full current flows to motor; armature cranks engine
1 mark: (a) roller/overrun clutch protects armature when engine fires
1 mark: (a) key released: spring returns plunger and pinion
2 marks: (b) axial: whole armature moves axially to engage pinion (sliding armature)
2 marks: (b) inertia: pinion moves on helix by its inertia; armature does not slide
4 marks: (c) any four: flat battery, loose/corroded terminals, faulty solenoid, worn brushes, burnt commutator, open armature/field, faulty ignition switch (1 each)
questions.explanation: Key on: solenoid pulls plunger, lever shifts pinion into mesh, contacts close, motor cranks; overrun clutch protects; release returns all. Axial starters move the armature; inertia starters throw the pinion on a helix. Faults: flat battery, poor connections, solenoid, brushes, commutator, windings, switch.

questions.topic: Construction and operation of ignition coil
questions.stem:
(a) Describe the internal construction of a conventional ignition coil. [5 marks]
(b) Explain how the coil produces a high voltage when the contact breaker opens. [6 marks]
(c) State the function of the capacitor in the contact-breaker system. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) laminated soft iron core
1 mark: (a) secondary winding of many thousand turns of fine wire wound next to core
1 mark: (a) primary winding of a few hundred turns of thicker wire outside
1 mark: (a) windings insulated, case filled with oil/compound
1 mark: (a) terminals: LT +/− and HT tower
2 marks: (b) current in primary builds magnetic field in core
2 marks: (b) points open, primary current stops, field collapses rapidly
2 marks: (b) collapsing field cuts secondary turns inducing high voltage (mutual induction, turns ratio)
2 marks: (c) reduces arcing/burning at the points
2 marks: (c) speeds collapse of the field, giving higher secondary voltage
questions.explanation: The coil has a laminated core, fine secondary and thick primary windings in an oil-filled can. Primary current builds a field; when points open it collapses quickly, inducing a high secondary voltage by mutual induction. The capacitor stops arcing at points and makes collapse faster.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four components of a charging system and state the function of each. [8 marks]
(b) Describe how to test whether an alternator is charging, using a voltmeter. [4 marks]
(c) State three causes of alternator bearing failure. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) alternator: generates electrical energy
2 marks: (a) regulator: controls output voltage
2 marks: (a) battery: stores energy and stabilises voltage
2 marks: (a) warning lamp/switch/cables: indicate charge, connect circuit (any one)
1 mark: (b) measure battery voltage engine off (about 12.6 V)
1 mark: (b) start engine, raise to about 2000 rev/min
1 mark: (b) voltage should rise to about 13.8–14.5 V
1 mark: (b) no rise means not charging; too high means regulator fault
3 marks: (c) any three: belt over-tight, lack of lubrication, contamination by dirt/water, wear with age, misalignment (1 each)
questions.explanation: Alternator generates, regulator limits voltage, battery stores, lamp indicates. Voltmeter: about 12.6 V static, rising to 13.8–14.5 V at fast idle if charging. Bearings fail from over-tight belts, dirt, poor lubrication and age.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between obligatory and non-obligatory lights, giving two examples of each. [6 marks]
(b) Describe how head lamps can be set using a screen marked on a wall. [6 marks]
(c) State three causes of dim head lamps. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) obligatory: required by law
2 marks: (a) examples: head lamps, tail lamps, stop lamps, indicators, number plate lamp (any two)
1 mark: (a) non-obligatory: optional/accessory lights
2 marks: (a) examples: fog lamps, spot lamps, reversing lamp in some cases, interior lights (any two)
1 mark: (b) vehicle on level floor, unladen, correct tyre pressures
1 mark: (b) park at specified distance facing wall
1 mark: (b) mark centre lines of lamps on wall
1 mark: (b) mark cut-off line below lamp centre height as specified
2 marks: (b) switch on dipped beam and adjust screws until beam meets marks
3 marks: (c) any three: poor earth, corroded connections, low voltage/weak battery, dirty or discoloured reflectors, wrong bulb (1 each)
questions.explanation: Obligatory lights are required by law (head, tail, stop, indicators); others are optional (fog, spot). Screen setting: level vehicle at set distance, mark lamp centres and cut-off line, adjust beams. Dim lamps result from poor earths, corrosion, low voltage or dull reflectors.

questions.topic: Maintenance and repairs of auxiliary components
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the need for an auxiliary system in a motor vehicle. [3 marks]
(b) Describe the operation of a thermal-type water temperature gauge. [6 marks]
(c) The horn of a car does not sound when the horn button is pressed. Outline six checks you would carry out in a logical order. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) provides driver information (gauges), safety (horn, wipers, indicators) and comfort/convenience
2 marks: (b) sender unit in water jacket contains thermistor whose resistance falls as temperature rises
2 marks: (b) current through gauge heater coil increases, heating bimetal strip
2 marks: (b) bimetal bends, moving needle to higher reading; voltage stabiliser keeps reading steady
6 marks: (c) check fuse; check relay clicks; check supply at horn with test lamp; check horn earth; check button/earth contact; bridge relay to test horn directly; adjust or replace horn (1 each, logical order)
questions.explanation: Auxiliaries give information, safety and convenience. The sender thermistor resistance drops with heat, more current heats the gauge bimetal and moves the needle. Horn fault: fuse, relay, supply, earth, button, direct test, then adjust or replace the horn.
